Control parameters for zinbreg()

zinbreg_control.Rd

Tolerances and iteration limits for the EM algorithm used by zinbreg() and for the IRLS fits inside its M-steps.

Usage

zinbreg_control(
  tol = 1e-08,
  maxit = 1000,
  mstep_tol = 1e-10,
  mstep_maxit = 100,
  irls_tol = 1e-10,
  irls_maxit = 100,
  nr_tol = 1e-10,
  nr_maxit = 100,
  theta_max = 1e+08,
  theta_warn = 10000,
  trace = FALSE
)

Arguments

tol

EM tolerance on the absolute change in the observed-data log-likelihood. Default 1e-8.

maxit

Maximum number of EM iterations. Default 1000.

mstep_tol

Outer tolerance (absolute change in the weighted NB log-likelihood) for the count-part M-step. Default 1e-10.

mstep_maxit

Maximum number of outer iterations in the count-part M-step. Default 100.

irls_tol, irls_maxit

Tolerance (relative change in the log-likelihood) and iteration limit for the IRLS loops (both parts).

nr_tol, nr_maxit

Tolerance (step in \(\log\theta\)) and iteration limit for the Newton-Raphson update of \(\theta\).

theta_max, theta_warn

Upper bound for \(\theta\), and the value above which a warning about the Poisson limit is given; see nbreg_control().

trace

Logical. If TRUE, print the log-likelihood after each EM iteration.

Value

A list of control parameters.

Details

The EM algorithm stops when the observed-data log-likelihood changes by less than tol (absolute change). Each M-step is fitted to convergence: the zero-part logistic regression by IRLS (relative log-likelihood change below irls_tol), and the count part by the NB algorithm of nbreg() with outer tolerance mstep_tol.

See also

zinbreg(), nbreg_control()

Examples

zinbreg_control(tol = 1e-10, maxit = 2000)
#> $tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $maxit
#> [1] 2000
#> 
#> $mstep_tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $mstep_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $irls_tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $irls_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $nr_tol
#> [1] 1e-10
#> 
#> $nr_maxit
#> [1] 100
#> 
#> $theta_max
#> [1] 1e+08
#> 
#> $theta_warn
#> [1] 10000
#> 
#> $trace
#> [1] FALSE
#>
